signals.signal: UBB's own live branch/ATM locator API returns 738 ATM pins and 172 branch pins nationwide on 30/07/2026. This does NOT support the 937-ATM figure carried in the baseline; note pins are sites, so machine-level count may differ.
signals.implies: Correct sizing of the #1 Bulgarian bank's fleet: ~738 ATM sites vs 5,031 ATM terminals nationally (~15% share) - the single largest addressable ATM/self-service estate in Bulgaria for Printec ATM + managed services.
signals.likelihood: Fleet refresh cycle post-euro highly likely within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Ask UBB/KBC procurement for machine count vs site count and current OEM mix

signals.signal: Only 246 of the 738 ATM pins carry the 'cash deposit at ATM' feature (slug atm-money-deposit); 705 are flagged 24/7 access. Roughly two-thirds of the estate is cash-out only.
signals.implies: ~490 cash-out-only sites are direct recycler/deposit-automation white space - Printec cash automation and ATM/self-service upgrade.
signals.likelihood: High - post-euro cash-deposit demand is proven (see BGN 406m via deposit ATMs in H1-2026)
signals.followup: Pitch a recycler business case using UBB's own H1-2026 deposit volumes

signals.signal: The locator flags 34 branches as 'Euro Hub' (euro-hub, coin-counting machines), 5 as 'cashless branch' (Безкасов клон / cashless-service), 5 as joint UBB+KBC Bank branches, 3 with a public vault and 4 with extended hours.
signals.implies: Coin handling and the cashless-branch format are institutionalised categories in UBB's own network taxonomy - entry points for Printec coin recyclers, TCRs and branch self-service zones.
signals.likelihood: Coin-machine estate persists beyond the changeover; extension likely
signals.followup: Identify the coin-counting machine OEM at the 34 Euro Hubs

signals.signal: UBB press item of 27/01/2026 listed 33 'specially equipped Euro Hubs' with coin-counting machines for exchanges above 200 coins, spread over Sofia (11), Plovdiv (2), Varna (2), Burgas (2) and 18 other towns, alongside 9 branches opening on each of three Saturdays in January 2026.
signals.source_name: UBB news - Branches working overtime on Saturdays and Eurohubs for coins
signals.implies: Confirms the Eurohub concept and its footprint; the estate has since grown to 34 sites per the live locator.

signals.signal: KNOWN-STALE FLAG: the '>780 ATMs / one of the two largest networks in the country' statement still live on ubb.bg sits on a customer notice dated 05 September 2012. It must not be carried as a current figure, and no 2026 ATM count is published by UBB.
signals.source_name: UBB news - Office working hours and ATM availability on holidays
signals.implies: Both the 937 and the 780+ numbers in circulation are unusable; the locator is the only defensible current basis for sizing a proposal.
signals.followup: Request an official fleet number from UBB directly

signals.signal: Audited FY2025 statements: at 31/12/2025 the Bank operated through HQ plus 171 branches and 18 business centres (2024: 176 branches and 18 business centres); 3,901 full-time employees (2024: 3,914); UBB Group 3,924. Statements approved 21/04/2026.
signals.source_name: UBB AD Annual Report and Financial Statements 2025
signals.implies: Five net branch exits in a year with headcount flat - migration of counter work to self-service is the lever; supports a TCR/self-service-zone pitch rather than a pure branch-closure story.

signals.signal: FY2025 capital additions (separate): property & equipment BGN 26.766m of which 'equipment and other assets' BGN 24.105m, and intangible assets (software) BGN 22.284m. Depreciation policy lists 'Office machinery, servers, ATMs and POS' at 20% (5 years); ATM rentals are treated as low-value leases, i.e. part of the fleet is rented rather than owned.
signals.source_name: UBB AD Financial Statements 2025, Note 4.2 and accounting policies
signals.implies: An annual hardware envelope of roughly BGN 24m (c. EUR 12m) plus a stated willingness to lease ATMs - a direct opening for a Printec ATM-as-a-service / managed-services model with no capex for the bank.
signals.followup: Quantify the ATM rental component and who the lessor is

signals.signal: Six months after euro adoption (03/07/2026): 564,063 people visited UBB branches to deposit or exchange BGN; nearly BGN 2.3bn exchanged in the first five months (BGN 1.5bn in January alone); 370 tonnes of coins accepted; BGN 406m deposited through ATMs with a deposit function; 94% of BGN in circulation withdrawn by end-June.
signals.source_name: UBB news - Six months after the euro adoption
signals.implies: Hard evidence that the deposit-ATM channel absorbed only a small slice of a huge cash flow because capacity is limited to 246 sites - the strongest single business case for Printec recyclers and coin automation at UBB.
signals.followup: Build the branch-cost-per-transaction comparison for the sales pitch

signals.signal: UBB extended free deposits of BGN banknotes into euro accounts to 30/09/2026 (previously 31/12/2025 campaign); after that the standard retail tariff applies, with BNB continuing unlimited free exchange thereafter.
signals.source_name: UBB news - UBB extends the term to 30.09.2026 for free deposit of levs
signals.implies: Cash-handling load at branches and deposit ATMs stays elevated through Q3-2026 - a live window to sell interim cash-automation capacity.

signals.signal: New tiered daily-banking plans launched 30/06/2026 (Teen free, Youth EUR 0.50, Smart EUR 1.50-2.50 with 12 months free if activated by 31/12/2026, Smart+ EUR 3.00-4.00, Pension EUR 0.90); every tier includes free deposits at UBB ATMs, and several include free withdrawals at any bank's ATM nationwide.
signals.source_name: UBB news - UBB offers new daily banking plans
signals.implies: Pricing deliberately pushes cash deposits onto ATMs; volume growth without matching deposit-capable hardware creates queueing and availability pressure - a capacity argument for recyclers and for Printec managed services/SLA uptime.

signals.signal: FY2025 annual report: Kate handled c. 5.1 million client interactions, autonomy (requests resolved without human intervention) rose from 68% to 75%, covering work equal to c. 32 FTEs; UBB Mobile passed 1 million clients; C/I ratio improved to 41.9% from 46.2%. Stated 2026 emphasis is acceleration of digitalisation, process automation and innovation 'with particular focus on the capabilities of the core banking system (T24)', plus KATE 2.0 as a fully LLM-orchestrated assistant extending beyond UBB Mobile to web and internal channels.
signals.source_name: UBB AD Annual Report 2025 (CEO address and Strategic Focus)
signals.implies: Temenos T24 is the confirmed core; 2026 money goes to automation and channel integration - Printec's integration/managed-services and transaction-monitoring lines fit, hardware less so this cycle.
signals.followup: Identify the T24 systems integrator on the 2026 workstream

signals.signal: 62% of new UBB clients opened their account fully digitally without visiting a branch in Jan-May 2026, versus a market average of c. 30%; UBB Mobile reaches 74% of the client base with 60.2% monthly active; Kate is used by 71% of mobile users, 2.2m conversations Jan-May 2026, 75% relevant answers, 60,000 vignettes sold; DZI settles 67% of CASCO claims digitally with an AI damage-assessment tool cutting assessment from 48 hours to 30 minutes; InResto has 30,000+ users and EUR 2.25m assets.
signals.source_name: 24chasa.bg - Over half of UBB's new clients open their account digitally (UBB Open Demo Day)
signals.implies: Remote onboarding is already the dominant acquisition channel - the eKYC/digital-onboarding slot at UBB is filled, so Printec should target the AML/transaction-monitoring and fraud layer behind it rather than onboarding front-end.

signals.signal: KBC Group 1Q2026 company presentation: Bulgaria accounts for 5% of group assets, 2.2m clients, 170 bank branches, EUR 13bn loans / EUR 16bn deposits; Kate is live in BE, CZ and BG only with roll-out planned to SK and HU; group-wide 6.1m users, 420k converted leads in 12 months, autonomy quoted at 77% BE and 69% CZ; Kate 2.0 (LLM) has been upgraded in Belgium first.
signals.implies: Bulgaria is a full core market inside a 'build once, deploy everywhere' group IT model - local hardware/service decisions stay local, but software is group-mandated. Sell hardware, cash automation and field services locally; do not chase local software platforms.
signals.followup: Confirm the exact 1Q2026 publication date on kbc.com

signals.signal: UBB published its Verification of Payee (VoP) service on 15/07/2026: a 24/7/365 name-IBAN match check on SEPA credit transfers and instant payments in UBB Online and UBB Mobile, with four outcomes (match, close match, no match, check not possible). UBB states the service becomes mandatory for all banks in Bulgaria from 01/01/2027.
signals.implies: A hard 01/01/2027 compliance deadline across every Bulgarian bank - Printec's AML/compliance, fraud and transaction-monitoring lines have a dated window with the laggard banks, and UBB is already live so it is a reference not a prospect.
signals.followup: Map which Bulgarian banks are NOT yet VoP-live

signals.signal: UBB's merchant softPOS product 'DigiPOS' turns an Android 10+ NFC phone or tablet into a card-acceptance terminal (Visa/Mastercard contactless), with free remote installation, free maintenance, updates and staff training, an electronic transaction-monitoring portal, and settlement in 1 business day for domestic-issued cards / 3 for foreign. Alongside physical and virtual POS it forms UBB's acquiring line-up.
signals.implies: UBB already has a softPOS answer, so a Printec POS pitch has to be about physical terminal estate, deployment/managed services and PCI-compliant key management (HSM) rather than a me-too softPOS app.
signals.followup: Identify the DigiPOS technology partner (tapXphone is referenced in secondary sources but is not named on the UBB page)

signals.signal: BNB payment statistics: ATM terminals in Bulgaria fell to 5,031 at end-2025 (5,087 end-2024; 5,128 end-2023), while POS terminals jumped to 210,861 (163,190 end-2024, +29% y/y); debit cards 7.92m, credit cards 1.389m.
signals.source_name: Bulgarian National Bank - Main indicators of payment statistics for Bulgaria (XLSX, EUR series)
signals.implies: National ATM estate is shrinking c.1%/yr while acceptance explodes: the ATM opportunity in Bulgaria is replacement/upgrade to recyclers, not net growth. UBB's ~738 sites are c.15% of the national estate.
signals.followup: Pull the H1-2026 half-year release when published

signals.signal: On 13/06/2025 UBB suffered a day-long technical failure affecting card transactions, ATM withdrawals and POS terminals; the bank confirmed disruption in the morning and only announced full restoration in the evening, extending branch opening hours during the incident. Press reporting attributed it to cards issued by UBB before the merger with Raiffeisenbank Bulgaria; UBB did not publish a root cause.
signals.source_name: UBB news - Temporary technical difficulties with some card transactions have been resolved
signals.implies: A documented single-day outage across the whole card/ATM/POS chain is the opening for Printec managed services, monitoring and availability SLAs on the self-service estate.
signals.followup: Check whether any regulatory/DORA incident report followed

signals.signal: UBB won the 'Market Share' award of the Bank of the Year Association for the second consecutive year (announced 24/06/2026) and a special diploma for 'Best Bank Digital Project' for its Kate-orchestrated digital housing ecosystem and Blink donations via Kate; it also took a hat-trick at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence including Best Digital Bank in Bulgaria and a fourth consecutive Best ESG Bank.
signals.source_name: UBB news - UBB with the award for largest market share for a second consecutive year
signals.implies: Confirms UBB as the #1 reference account in Bulgaria - winning here is a lighthouse for the whole market, which justifies aggressive commercial terms on a first recycler tranche.

coverage_notes: Fresh run (no checkpoint existed). Primary-first: UBB's own live locator JSON endpoint (discovered by scraping the /offices page for the form action /locations/pins), UBB AD Annual Report + Financial Statements 2025 (PDF extracted locally with pdfminer), UBB Local Report to Society 2025 PDF, six pages of the ubb.bg news index in Bulgarian (dates read from the page DOM, not from search snippets), KBC Group 1Q2026 company presentation PDF, and the BNB payment-statistics XLSX. Searched in both English and Bulgarian and deliberately entered through the locator API, the KBC IR document tree and the BNB statistics files rather than re-walking the pages the baseline used. VERIFIED AND CORRECTED: the 937-ATM baseline figure is unsupported - the locator shows 738 ATM pins; and the '>780 ATMs' line still on ubb.bg is a 05/09/2012 page. Branch count triangulates cleanly at 170-172 (KBC 1Q2026 says 170, audited FY2025 says 171 branches + 18 business centres, locator shows 172 pins). GENUINE GAPS: (1) the ATM/coin-machine OEM at UBB is still unidentified - UBB is privately held so there is no public procurement register, no vendor press release or case study names UBB, and the financial statements only disclose 'Office machinery, servers, ATMs and POS' as a depreciation class; (2) locator pins are sites, so a site with two machines is counted once - the true machine count is likely somewhat above 738 and could plausibly approach the 780-900 range, but nothing published supports 937; (3) no 2026 announcement of an ATM refresh or deposit-ATM expansion programme was found in any language; (4) KBC 2Q2026 results were not yet published at the time of this run (KBC's 1Q2026 set is the latest).
access_issues: dnevnik.bg returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch and a Cloudflare interstitial to a desktop-User-Agent curl, so the June-2025 outage was sourced from UBB's own dated news page instead (logged, not silently dropped). www.ubb.bg/news returned 301 to a redirect chain on the bare path; the working index is /news/index and /news/index/page:N. A POST to /locations/pins was rejected by the Akamai edge with HTTP 411; a plain GET on the same path returned the full 1.1MB JSON. No PDF was blocked: the UBB and KBC PDFs were downloaded with a browser User-Agent and text-extracted locally with pdfminer (pdftotext is not installed on this machine).
